lesson.text: Congruent shapes are exactly the same size and shape: one can be moved onto the other by translations, reflections and rotations.
Similar shapes have the same shape but may differ in size: a dilation (plus moves) takes one to the other.
In similar shapes, matching angles are equal and matching sides are in the same ratio: the scale factor.
Small triangle sides 3 and 5; big triangle's matching sides 6 and ?: the scale factor is 2, so ? = 10.

exercises.prompt: Congruent shapes are the same size and shape.
Which transformation can turn a shape into a similar but bigger one?
Similar triangles: small sides 3 and 5; big matching sides 6 and ?. What is the missing side?
Similar shapes have equal matching angles.
Similar rectangles: 4 cm by 6 cm, and 10 cm by ? cm. What is the missing side?
Two triangles have angles 40°, 60°, 80°. What must be true?
A 2 m pole casts a 3 m shadow. At the same time a tree casts a 12 m shadow. How tall is the tree, in metres?
A shape is reflected, then rotated. Is the result congruent to the start?
exercises.explain: Yes: size and shape stay the same.
